subject: Buyer criteria gap analysis & bake-off next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Barnes <ellie@medlytics.com>, Samir Patel <samir@medlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Buyer criteria gap analysis & bake-off next steps

Ellie / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Short recap from my side so we have a clear, actionable plan: 

Pain points you highlighted:
- High per-request token cost for long-context embeddings and reranking (primary blocker for scale).
- Sporadic hallucinations in clinical content that require human review workflows.
- Need for deterministic failover and audit trails for compliance (SOC 2 / data retention).
- Desire for predictable latency under peak load for synchronous search UX.

Goals we agreed on:
1) Reduce per-request costs by 30–50% via batching/quantization + model selection.
2) Demonstrate parity on clinical accuracy with a fixed evaluation set.
3) Provide a deployment option that meets data residency and audit log requirements.
4) Produce a decision matrix that maps candidate models/vendors to your criteria.

Proposed bake-off scope and next steps:
- We’ll run a head-to-head on a shared eval set (50 representative queries + 20 long-doc contexts).
- Redwood will provision a staging endpoint (dedicated capacity) and a fallback lightweight variant.
- Deliverables: competitive matrix (feature/perf/cost), pricing snapshot, and runbook for the tests.
- Timeline: staging access + matrix template by end of day Friday; run the tests early next week; brief sync after initial results.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_snapshot.pdf (pricing baseline) — I’ve also shared a blank matrix in Drive: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1aBcD_example_sheet

Open questions for your team:
- Can you confirm a) the list of 50 queries and b) who on your engineering team will run the tests?
- Any non-negotiable security controls beyond SOC 2 (e.g., HSM/KMS, private link)?

If that all looks right, I’ll get the staging endpoint ready and Marissa will drop the matrix workbook to you.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Buyer criteria gap analysis & bake-off next steps

Jonas —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- We can assemble the 50 queries by EOD Friday; Samir will own that.
- Security: SOC 2 is required, and we also need private VPC connectivity and customer-managed KMS for keys. If Redwood can support HSM-backed key storage in Private deployments, that would be ideal.
- Metrics to include in the matrix: avg latency (p95), tokens/response, top-1 clinical accuracy (judged by our SME), and audit-log completeness (events/sec and retention policy).

Samir wants the runbook to specify exact payload sizes and concurrency profiles — he’ll upload our latency targets in the shared sheet.

Can you also add a competitive column for 2 main vendors we’re evaluating? We’re tracking VertexCare and CloudInfer as the two alternatives — we want to see where Redwood is explicitly stronger or weaker.

Thanks — we’re good to proceed on the timeline you suggested.

Ellie
Ellie Barnes
